title: Assessment record
description:
A dated, human-accepted judgement about one security: what the thesis is, how ready it is to carry capital, and what the downside looks like. The thesis is the durable object; this is a photograph of it on one day.

What is NOT here matters as much as what is: no position weight, no cash, no P&L, no average cost, no contemplated trade. The research judgement is formed and frozen before its capital consequence is visible, so that a downside the owner would have to act on cannot quietly soften into one they would not.

A model can propose the content. Only a human can accept it, and accepting is recorded as an act with answers attached -- silently editing a number is not available. A factual error means rejecting the proposal; a different judgement means writing a human_authored assessment that links back to what it replaced.

thesis_id.description: Absent while underwriting a name that has no thesis yet.

assessment_mode.description: How much of the prior judgement was visible while forming this one. de_novo shows nothing (onboarding). update_against_prior requires the previous judgement, to measure change. independent_then_reconcile forms the view blind and explains the difference afterwards -- for material breaks, where anchoring costs the most.

readiness.description: Readiness is not conviction. It is a claim about the state of the evidence: an accepted thesis, a stated downside, an approved monitoring contract, no material data gap. watchlist carries no capital at all.

downside.description: The scenario that sizes the position. 'unknown' is a legitimate answer with a consequence: policy makes the name ineligible for new risk rather than guessing a number.

return_fraction.description: Negative fraction of the current price, e.g. '-0.3' for a 30% fall. Not basis points and not a percentage: this is a measured quantity, not a policy threshold.

reason.description: Why the downside cannot be stated. Required when status is unknown.

evidence_date.description: The date of the newest evidence this judgement rests on -- not the date it was written. A judgement written today on a filing from March is three months old, and the preview screen says so.

source_artifact.description: The skill output this judgement was formed against, when there was one.

human_authored.description: true when the owner wrote the judgement rather than accepting a proposal. Not a quality mark -- a provenance fact.

derived_from.description: The assessment this one replaces or updates. Set when a human-authored judgement supersedes a model proposal, so the disagreement stays visible instead of being overwritten.

acceptance.description: The act of accepting, with its answers. Skipping the questions is representable -- as acknowledged_without_full_adjudication, which does not count as adjudicated and cannot raise readiness.

would_accept_downside_without_position.description: 'If you did not already own this, would you accept the same downside?' A false answer does not void the record -- it blocks the record from supporting an increase in risk.

main_change_driver.description: What actually changed since the previous accepted judgement. Required whenever there is a previous one.

rationale.description: Required on a material change: a readiness move, or a downside difference over 500 bp.

allOf.$comment: Skipping the review is allowed but cannot masquerade as having done it.
An update has to say what it is updating, otherwise the mode is decoration.
